description.text: A hulking amphibious predator of lightless underground water, heavy through the body and smooth as an eel, with three stacked eyes and four long tentacles that it drags itself along on when it leaves the shallows. It thinks in inherited memory older than most civilisations, speaks mind to mind, and regards the surface and everyone on it as livestock.

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (11): thrust 1d cutting (KYOS: 2d+2 cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Tentacle
attacks.notes: Tentacle (11): thrust 3d-1 crushing (KYOS: 5d+1 crushing), Reach C-3.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (11): thrust 4d-1 crushing (KYOS: 7d crushing), Reach C-2. Can only attack rear hexes. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Mucus Cloud
attacks.notes: When underwater, the aboleth exudes a mucus cloud. Any creature in the same hex as the aboleth that breathes in the mucus must make a successful HT roll or lose the ability to breathe air and gain that ability to breathe water for 30 minutes times the margin of failure.

traits: Dependency (Water; Constantly; Enters hibernation after losing 1xHP)
Extra Legs (Four Legs; Cannot Kick; Extra-Flexible; Long 1)
Likes eating victims transformed by slime
Weakness (Immersion in saline water, 1d per 30 minutes)

description.text: A flightless bird the size of a warhorse, walking on four stiff obsidian legs with a compact armoured body slung between them. It keeps to burnt, sulfur-smelling country where organised cruelty is ordinary, kills with a hooked beak and heavy claws, and takes its time about it.

attacks.name: Sharp Beak
attacks.notes: Sharp Beak (14): thrust 2d+1 large piercing (KYOS: 3d+3 large piercing), Reach C.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws
attacks.notes: Sharp Claws (14): thrust 2d+1 cutting (KYOS: 3d+3 cutting), Reach C-1.

attacks.name: Black Cloud
attacks.notes: By spending 2 FP and performing a Ready maneuver, an achaierai can release a choking, toxic black cloud. It spreads in a 2-yard radius area around the achaierai, lasts 10 seconds, and drifts with the wind. The cloud imposes a -3 penalty on all vision- and Infravision-based rolls within the area. Additionally, every creature that inhales the cloud must make an HT roll. If it fails, it takes 1d toxic damage, ignoring DR, and begins to hallucinate for margin of failure minutes. After that the subject is stunned (p. B420) and may roll vs. HT once per second to recover. Achaierais are immune to this ability.

traits: Regeneration (Slow; Accessibility, Only legs and feet)

description.text: What is left of someone who died insane: a tattered upper body trailing away into smoke, no legs beneath it, hands drawn out too long. It cannot form words, only a rising babble that scatters thought, and its touch leaves the living hallucinating. Religious symbols drive it back.

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.notes: Punch (11): thrust 1d-4 crushing (KYOS: 1d-5 crushing), Reach C. Only against insubstantial targets.

attacks.name: Touch of Insanity
attacks.notes: Despite being insubstantial, allips can cause temporary insanity with their touch. Any living creature that touches an allip must make a Will roll (Mind Shield provides a bonus to resist, but DR does not) or begin to hallucinate for margin of failure minutes.

attacks.name: Babble
attacks.notes: When a creature hears the allip’s constant babble, it must roll a Fright Check using the Confusion table (GURPS Powers, p. 85). If a victim succeeds at his Fright Check, he will be unaffected by this ability for one hour.

attacks.name: Madness
attacks.notes: When a creature reads the mind of an allip or senses its emotions – by any method, including powers, spells, and unmodified advantages, it must roll a Fright Check. If a victim succeeds at his Fright Check, he will be unaffected by this ability for one hour.

description.text: A six-legged burrowing arthropod as heavy as a pony, with shovel-like foreclaws and mandibles that run with digestive acid. Nearly blind and completely deaf, it hunts by the tremor of footsteps overhead, erupting out of tilled soil to seize whatever is passing and drag it under.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws

attacks.name: Spit Acid
attacks.damage: 2d corrosion. Ranged attack (Acc 3, Range 20). Double the actual distance to the target when calculating the range modifier due to the ankheg being nearsighted. description.text: A feathered, legless hunter of the open air, built like a barbed dart with a hooked beak at the front and a rudder of a tail behind. It never lands willingly, spits arcs of lightning at range, and treats anything sharing its sky as an intruder to be driven off.

attacks.name: Sharp Beak
attacks.notes: Sharp Beak (15): thrust 1d-1 large piercing (KYOS: 1d-4 large piercing), Reach C.

attacks.name: Electricity Ray
attacks.damage: The arrowhawk fires forth a coruscating beam of electricity from its tail that does 2d burning surge damage. The attack has Acc 3 and Range 20/100. Metallic armor counts as DR 1 against this attack, but nonmetallic armor protects normally. Targets stuck by this attack must make an HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of injury, or be physically stunned. On subsequent turns, they can roll HT to recover. The charge of electricity can be dodged, but not blocked or parried. This attack behaves unpredictably around conductors; see Lightning (GURPS Magic, p. 196) for more details

description.text: A sphere of steady white-gold light no bigger than a helm, with no body to speak of: no face, no limbs, nothing an ordinary weapon can find. It drifts rather than walks, answers questions honestly and at some length, and fights fiends with lances of focused light while refusing to harm anyone innocent.

attacks.name: Light Ray
attacks.damage: 1d tight-beam burning. Ranged attack (Acc 3, Range 10). Costs 1 FP per use. Cannot affect holy beings. The beam is easily reflected. Normally it cannot be blocked, but someone may use a mirror or a highly polished shield to do so; this causes the attack to bounce off in a random direction, possibly striking the wrong target (p. B389). The mirror-wielder may even attempt to reflect it back at the archon, but this gives -2 to Block; the archon defends normally. On the upside, the archon may make use of mirrored surfaces to “ricochet” the beam. This inflicts -2 per bounce to the attack roll, but may allow the attacker to bypass cover; in addition, the target is at -1 per bounce to defend

description.text: A low, heavy lizard about as long as a man is tall, running on eight short legs, rough-scaled in olive and ochre with a blunt wedge of a head. It is slow, ill-tempered and entirely unhurried, because it has no need of speed: whatever meets its glowing amber eyes stops being flesh.

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (10): thrust 1d+1 cutting (KYOS: 2d cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Petrifying Gaze
attacks.damage: A basilisk’s petrifying gaze spreads out in a cone 15 yards long and 15 yards wide at the end. It can select who is affected; potential victims must be looking at it. For every target, there is a Quick Contest between the basilisk’s Will (minus a range penalty taken from the Speed/Range Table) and each target’s HT. If the basilisk wins, the target is petrified. (The distinction between “paralyzed” and “petrified” generally works in their victims’ favor – e.g., they won’t starve – so the basilisk does not pay extra for this.) Someone looking at a reflection of a basilisk is not affected by its gaze. Fighting while looking in a mirror is at a -5 penalty; attacks made with closed eyes are at -10. Petrification can be removed with Remove Curse or Stone to Flesh. This attack also affects insubstantial beings

attacks.name: Chains

attacks.notes: Chains (15): The chain devil has two long chains that it can use to attack enemies. These chains deal swing 2d crushing, Reach 1-4*. The chains are awkward enough that they require a Ready maneuver to change reach (e.g., between 1 and 3). Otherwise, the chain devil can strike at foes that are at any distance within the chains’ reach. Attempts to parry the chains are at -4, and fencing weapons cannot parry at all! Attempts to block chains are at -2. This swinging attack is unbalanced – the chain devil cannot use it to parry if it has already used it to attack this turn (or vice versa), and parries with the chains are at -2. The chain devil has two chain attacks, which permits him Dual-Weapon Attacks (p. B417). The chains have DR 4 and effective weight 1.4 lbs. This attack uses the Kusari skill.

attacks.name: Dancing Chains
attacks.damage: The chain devil can animate any chain within 10 yards of him. He can animate up to 8 yards of chain, assuming the chain weighs 2 lbs. per yard. 8 yards of chain have 20 HP. An animated chain can grab, lift, strike, and throw with ST equal to its HP/2. It has the chain devil’s DX. It can walk and jump if it isn’t fixed in place; Move equals 10–HP/2. The chain devil can use skills through animated chains (including Kusari to make swinging attacks) – but note that chains have No Fine Manipulators. Chains return to their rest state once the chain devil gives up control

description.text: A headless, legless mass that slithers on a broad tapered underside and does not hold any shape long enough to describe twice. Limbs and claws surface where it needs them. Transformation magic slides off something already refusing to have a form, and its touch leaves a body unsure what shape it is meant to be.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws
attacks.notes: Sharp Claws (12): thrust 1d+1 cutting (KYOS: 2d cutting), Reach C. If a living takes damage from the chaos beast’s claws, it must make a HT check to resist a transformative effect. Its body transforms into an amorphous mass for margin of failure minutes. Its Basic Move is reduced by 2, it gains Injury Tolerance (Homogenous, No Blood, No Head, No Neck), Invertebrate, Mute, No Legs (Slithers), and No Manipulators. It cannot wear any armor or use any items in this state - they all become useless and fall from the victim’s body. In addition, the victim constantly experiences terrible pain (p. B428). The victim can negate this effect and return to its natural form by taking a Concentrate maneuver a making a successful Will-4 roll. If successful, he retains his shape until the end of his next turn.

attacks.damage: Once per hour the vrock can emit a screech that stuns every non-demon everyone in a cone-shaped area. Cones use special rules; see Area and Spreading Attacks (p. B413). attacks.notes: Stunning Screech (14): Once per hour the vrock can emit a screech that stuns every non-demon everyone in a cone-shaped area. Cones use special rules; see Area and Spreading Attacks (p. attacks.name: Spores
attacks.notes: Once every 15 seconds the vrock can emit a 2-yard radius cloud of spores around himself. This requires a Concentrate maneuver and costs 1 FP. The spores work as a contact agent, ignoring unsealed DR and dealing 1 point of toxic damage every 10 seconds for 6 cycles total. At the end of this time, the victim is covered with a tangle of viny growths. The vines are harmless and wither away in 1d4 days. The spores can be removed with a successful Physician roll (takes 10 seconds). Bless, neutralize poison, or remove disease kills the spores, as does sprinkling the victim with a vial of holy water.

attacks.name: Dance of Ruin
attacks.notes: To use this ability, a group of at least three vrocks must join hands in a circle, dancing wildly and chanting. At the end of 16 seconds of dancing, a wave of crackling energy flashes outward in a 32-yard radius. All creatures except for demons within the radius take 6d crushing damage. This affects even insubstantial creatures. Stunning, paralyzing, or slaying one of the vrocks stops the dance. The dance costs each vrock 2 FP.

attacks.name: Entangle
attacks.damage: Each erinyes carries a stout rope some 50 feet long that entangles anyone it strikes. The erinyes uses Whip skill for this attack. It is treated as a melee attack with a range equal to the rope’s length, but not more than 20 yards. On a hit, the victim is grappled (see p. B370) and rooted in place. He cannot select the Move or Change Posture maneuvers or change facing, and is at -4 to DX. The ST of this effect is equal to 10. To break free, the victim must win a Quick Contest of ST or Escape skill against 10. Each attempt takes one second. If the victim fails to break free, he loses 1 FP but may try again. Alternatively, he may try to destroy the rope. Innate Attacks hit automatically; other attacks are at -4. External attacks on the rope take no penalty, but risk hitting the victim on a miss (see Striking Into a Close Combat, p. B392). The rope has DR 3. Each point of damage reduces ST by one. At ST 0, the rope is destroyed and the victim is freed

description.text: A vast segmented worm sheathed in blue-white ice armour, eyeless, with a ring of fangs opening directly in the front of its body. It lies buried in snow, indistinguishable from a drift, and breathes a cold that kills outright. Its trilling call leaves anything that hears it standing still and stupid.

attacks.name: Fangs
attacks.notes: Fangs (11): thrust 6d impaling (KYOS: 7d impaling), Reach C.

attacks.name: Breathe Frost
attacks.damage: The worm breathes out a blast of extremely cold vapor, dealing thrust 4d-1 non-incendiary burning damage (KYOS: 4d) as large-area injury. Targets injured by this attack must make an HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of injury, or take a -2 penalty to DX and become Numb (p. B146) for (20-HT) minutes (minimum 1 minute). This is a cone attack that uses rules from Area and Spreading Attacks (pp. B413-414). The cone is 1-yard wide and has a length of 9 yards (ST/5). Each use costs 2 FP. It is possible to make the cone wider by using the rules from Cones of Power (GURPS Dungeon Fantasy Monsters 4: Dragons, p. 10). It will blow out any ordinary fire (candle, lantern, torch, etc.)

attacks.name: Death Throes
attacks.notes: When killed, a frost worm turns to ice and shatters in an explosion that deals 6d non-incendiary burning explosive damage and releases [1d] impaling fragments that can damage anyone within 5 yards. Targets injured by this attack must make an HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of injury, or take a -2 penalty to DX and become Numb (p. B146) for (20-HT) minutes (minimum 1 minute).

attacks.name: Trill
attacks.notes: A frost worm can emit a noise that forces its prey to stand motionless. This effect affects all creatures other than frost worms within a 32-yard radius. Creatures must succeed on a Will roll or be dazed (p. B428) for 3 seconds times margin of failure. After that each subject is stunned (p. B420) and may roll vs. Will once per second to recover. Victims must be able to hear the trill to be affected. Using the trill costs 1 FP.

attacks.notes: Spiked Chains (16): The zelekhut can take a Ready maneuver to unfurl spiked chains from his forearms or to retract them back. These chains deal swing 2d crushing, Reach 1-4*. The chains are awkward enough that they require a Ready maneuver to change reach (e.g., between 1 and 3). Otherwise, the zelekhut can strike at foes that are at any distance within the chains’ reach. Attempts to parry the chains are at -4, and fencing weapons cannot parry at all! Attempts to block chains are at -2. This swinging attack is unbalanced – the zelekhut cannot use it to parry if he have already used it to attack this turn (or vice versa), and parries with the chains are at -2. The zelekhut has two chain attacks, which permits him Dual-Weapon Attacks (p. B417). Spikes favor disarming, giving the zelekhut a +2 on disarming attempts. The chains have DR 4 and effective weight 0.84 lbs. This attack uses the Kusari skill.

monsters.pageRef: Ice Mephit (Enraged Eggplant; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)

description.text: A faceted mephit of pale blue ice with frost-white rime wings, cold enough to hurt to stand beside. It breathes a spray of shards, it is as brittle as it looks in places, and it is easily the most sneering of a family not known for manners.

attacks.name: Blunt Claws
attacks.notes: Blunt Claws (13): thrust 1d-2 crushing (KYOS: 1d-5 crushing), Reach C.

attacks.name: Breath Weapon
attacks.damage: A 10-yard jet of ice shards erupts from the mephit’s mouth. It uses Innate Attack (Breath) to hit. Don’t apply range penalties; treat this as a long melee weapon rather than a ranged attack. It does 1d small piercing damage, and has a 1/2D range of 5 yards. If any damage penetrates the target’s DR, he must make a HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of injury or suffer a -2 penalty to DX for (20 – HT) minutes as his skin and eyes numb. This ability costs 1 FP to use
attacks.notes: Breath Weapon (13): A 10-yard jet of ice shards erupts from the mephit’s mouth. It uses Innate Attack (Breath) to hit. Don’t apply range penalties; treat this as a long melee weapon rather than a ranged attack. It does 1d small piercing damage, and has a 1/2D range of 5 yards. If any damage penetrates the target’s DR, he must make a HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of injury or suffer a -2 penalty to DX for (20 – HT) minutes as his skin and eyes numb. This ability costs 1 FP to use.

attacks.name: Chill Metal
attacks.notes: By spending 3 FP, an ice mephit can spend 1 FP to use this ability on a metal object, making it very cold to the touch. This ability is resolved as a Quick Contest of the mephit's Will vs. the object's HT, penalized for range normally. It deals 1 point of burning damage per second to everyone touching it. This damage comes from extreme cold, not heat, so it cannot set anything on fire. Targets injured by this ability must make an HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of injury, or take a -2 penalty to DX and become Numb (p. B146) for (20-HT) minutes (minimum 1 minute). Useful when used on foe’s plate armor or metal weapon.

traits: Regeneration (Fast; Accessibility, Only if the ambient temperature is 32°F or below)

description.text: A wiry blue-black crone with coarse iron-grey hair, pointed ears and long black claws, wearing a dark red heartstone on an iron chain. She walks into sleep the way other people walk into a room, and rides a sleeper night after night until there is nothing left to ride.

attacks.name: Fangs
attacks.notes: Fangs (13): thrust 1d-1 impaling (KYOS: 1d impaling), Reach C. Any victim that takes damage from this attack risks contacting demon fever. After an incubation period of 1d days, he must make a HT-4 roll or take 1d-2 toxic damage. Every day for 4 more cycles he must make another HT-4 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/3 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -2 penalty to HT until he heals above this threshold. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim begins to cough (p. B428) until he heals above this threshold. This disease is mildly contagious, as per Illness (p. B442).

attacks.name: Dream Haunting
attacks.damage: Night hags can visit the dreams of sleeping individuals, turning them into nightmares. This ability works at a distance. Each second, roll a Quick Contest of Will (or Dreaming, if better, for both sides). The night hag is at -1 per yard of distance. Each victory lets her drain 1 FP. The night hag heals 1 HP per full 3 FP she steals. Treat FP lost to this ability as FP lost to missed sleep for all purposes

description.text: A black horse with a mane of red-orange flame and fire cuffing each hoof, leaving scorch marks where it stands. It flies, it does not tire, and it trails a choking smoke that blinds anyone trying to close with its rider.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (12): thrust 2d+1 crushing (KYOS: 3d crushing) + 1d-1 follow-up burning, Reach C-1. Flaming Hooves: Burning Attack 1d-1 (Follow-Up, Hooves, +0%; Magical, -10%) Resolve as stated by the construction; the source gives no separate resolution text.

attacks.name: Fangs
attacks.notes: Fangs (12): thrust 1d-1 impaling (KYOS: 2d-1 impaling), Reach C.

attacks.name: Astral Projection
attacks.damage: The nightmare can leave its body behind, unconscious, while projecting its spirit to the Astral Plane by making an IQ roll and spending 1 FP. While there, it cannot cast spells or otherwise affect the world in any meaningful way. The spirit form is visible, but insubstantial. This ability can be maintained indefinitely, provided the nightmare continues paying 1 FP per minute, but the body’s need to eat, drink, sleep, etc. effectively limits the duration to a day or so – longer if the body is left with friends, or otherwise cared for

attacks.name: Smoke
attacks.damage: The nightmare may fill a two-yard-radius area within 10 yards with bad smelling smoke. This gives -3 to all vision and Infravision rolls made through it. description.text: A shapeless mass of viscous black matter that pours along walls and ceilings as easily as floors, and weighs several tons. It is blind, mindless and entirely without organs, so there is nothing on it to aim at; what it flows over, it digests.

attacks.name: Engulf (Binding ST 24)
attacks.notes: No attack roll is necessary; the quarry may defend only by dodging and retreating. Moving through an SM+2 or smaller creature is an automatic slam. A victim who fails to dodge is pinned if smaller than the pudding, or grappled if equal or larger. Breaking free is a Quick Contest of ST (only every 10 seconds if pinned; on a 17 or 18 the victim cannot escape unaided); the pudding has +10 ST when pinning and +5 when grappling. Engulfed victims cannot breathe and begin to suffocate when out of breath. It can pin or grapple one foe at a time; others are pushed along in front of it unless they win a Quick Contest of ST. It may constrict an engulfed victim every turn at effective ST 24.

attacks.name: Acid (Corrosion Aura)
attacks.notes: Always on, no attack roll. Any organic or metal creature or object touching the pudding takes 1d-1 corrosion per second; stone is unaffected. Engulfed creatures and objects take it as large-area injury. Selective, so it does not destroy what the pudding is not attacking.

traits: Injury Tolerance (Homogenous, No Blood, No Eyes, No Head, No Neck)

attacks.name: Dagger

attacks.name: Horns

attacks.notes: Short Bow (13): thrust 1d-2 impaling, Acc 1, Range 150/200, RoF 1, Shots 1(2).

attacks.name: Fear
attacks.notes: The satyr can play a frightening tune that forces creatures who hear it (the satyr can exlude any creatures it does not want to affect) to roll an immediate Fright Check (p. B360).

attacks.name: Sleep
attacks.notes: This tune makes creatures within 8 yards that hear it fall asleep for margin of failure minutes, if they fail to resist in a Quick Contest of the satyr’s Musical Instrument (Pan Pipes) skill against their Will. After this, they can be woken normally, but they will not necessarily wake up right away, especially if already tired. Upon waking up, each subject is stunned (p. B420) and may roll vs. Will once per second to recover. The satyr can omit any creatures from the effect.

description.text: A small blue-grey lizard, harmless-looking and about the length of a forearm, that clings to cave walls in colonies. It senses living things by the charge on them and delivers a shock; several of them together can put a grown adult on the ground.

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (14): thrust 1d-5 cutting (KYOS: 1d-8 cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Passive Electroreception
attacks.damage: See GURPS Powers: Enhanced Senses, p. 17
attacks.notes: Passive Electroreception (12): See GURPS Powers: Enhanced Senses, p. 17.

attacks.name: Stunning Shock
attacks.damage: Once per 5 seconds, the shocker lizard can create an electrical discharge that has a chance to stun an enemy. This is a ranged attack with 1/2D 10, Max 100, Acc 3, RoF 1, Shots N/A, and Recoil 1. It works at 1/10 of its range underwater. A struck victim must make an immediate HT roll with a bonus equal to half of his DR. The victim gets a further +3 if he is beyond 1/2D range. If the victim makes his HT roll, he is unaffected. If he fails, he is stunned (see p. B420). He may roll vs. HT once per second to recover (DR has no effect on this roll)
attacks.notes: Stunning Shock (14): Once per 5 seconds, the shocker lizard can create an electrical discharge that has a chance to stun an enemy. This is a ranged attack with 1/2D 10, Max 100, Acc 3, RoF 1, Shots N/A, and Recoil 1. It works at 1/10 of its range underwater. A struck victim must make an immediate HT roll with a bonus equal to half of his DR. The victim gets a further +3 if he is beyond 1/2D range. If the victim makes his HT roll, he is unaffected. If he fails, he is stunned (see p. B420). He may roll vs. HT once per second to recover (DR has no effect on this roll).

attacks.name: Lethal Shock
attacks.notes: Once per 5 seconds, whenever a shocker lizard has two other shocker lizards within 4 yards, it can create a lethal shock in a 4-yard-radius area around itself. This shock deals 2d burning surge damage and can work underwater. Targets stuck by this attack must make an HT roll, at -1 per 2 points of penetrating damage, or be physically stunned. On subsequent turns, they can roll HT to recover.

description.text: A shelled sea creature the size of a large dog, with pincer arms and a hard case pierced by openings it shifts its limbs between. It sees in every direction at once, swims fast, and squirts a blinding ink before it decides whether to fight.

attacks.name: Pincers
attacks.notes: Pincers (13): thrust 1d-3 cutting (KYOS: 1d-4 cutting), Reach C. The tojanida can either nip and let go or hold on and grapple the victim in addition to injuring him. Either is an attack that takes full hit location penalties – not halved for grappling. Treat this attack as a bite for these purposes (see Teeth on page 115 of GURPS Martial Arts for details). The pincers give +2 with tasks that require a firm grip (including climbing).

attacks.name: Sharp Teeth
attacks.notes: Sharp Teeth (13): thrust 1d-3 cutting (KYOS: 1d-4 cutting), Reach C.

attacks.name: Ink
attacks.damage: A tojanida may fill a two-yard-radius area with black ink. No one can see into the affected area, and no one within the affected area can see anything; see p. B394 for combat rules. In addition, this ink cloud imposes a -4 penalty on Smell rolls. Once created, the cloud persists for 10 seconds, drifting with the current. This cloud can only be used in water or in zero-G. When used on land, this attack takes a form of an ink jet, which can strike any target up to 20 yards away (without range or speed penalties). It can be dodged or blocked, but not parried. If the jet strikes the face, it causes no injury, but blinds the target for 3 seconds unless he makes a successful HT roll. Thick goggles, closed helmets, ultra-tech visors protect against this spell. A tojanida can use this ability only 4 times per day

attacks.name: Kiss
attacks.damage: A vargouille can kiss a target by making a successful unarmed attack against the target’s unprotected face. An affected opponent must succeed on a HT roll or begin a terrible transformation that turns the creature into a vargouille within 24 hours (and often much sooner; roll 1d separately for each phase of the transformation). First, over a period of 1d hours, all the victim’s hair falls out. Within another 1d hours thereafter, the ears grow into leathery wings, tentacles sprout on the chin and scalp, and the teeth become long, pointed fangs. During the next 1d hours, the victim takes loses 1 IQ each hour (maximum 3). The transformation is complete 1d hours later, when the subject experiences a heart attack and, if not resuscitated, the head breaks free of the body (which promptly dies) and becomes a vargouille. This transformation is interrupted by sunlight (it can delay death), but to reverse the transformation requires Cure Disease at -3 or Remove Curse. Dispel Magic will not lift this effect

attacks.name: Sonic Lance
attacks.damage: Once per 5 seconds, a yrthak can focus sonic enery in a ray. This is a ranged attack with Acc 3 and Range 10/100 that costs 1 FP. The ray deals 4d burning non-incendiary damage. The attack produces an explosion at the point of impact (on a miss, check for scatter; see p. B414). The target takes damage normally; anything nearby receives “collateral damage” equal to basic damage divided by (3 x distance in yards from the blast). If the attack hits the ground, a large rock, a stone wall, or the like, it creates an explosion of shattered stone. Everyone within 5 yards is attacked with effective skill 15, modified by range penalties from the point of impact; see Fragmentation Damage (p. B414). The fragments deal 1d large piercing damage

monsters.name: Crocodile
monsters.pageRef: Crocodile (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A mud bank above a slow river, with a scraped nest hollow and a slide worn down into the water.

description.text: Thirteen feet of armored reptile lying in the shallows, looking exactly like a waterlogged log. It takes prey at the water's edge, drags it under and drowns it, and its hide turns a spear that would go through anything short of a dragon. On land it is slow enough to outrun. In the water it is not losing.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Closes and holds; the crocodile does not let go to bite again.

attacks.name: Death Roll
attacks.notes: Death Roll: Reach C. Against a target it already has in its jaws, the crocodile rolls its whole body. No attack roll; the victim rolls ST or DX to break the grip or is dragged under and drowned.

notes: Racial cost: -28 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5; water Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Frog
monsters.lair: Reed beds and pond margins; in a dry season, whatever mud is still damp.

description.text: An ordinary pond frog, present by the hundred in any wetland and no danger to anything larger than a moth. Frogs matter at the table as familiars, as spell components, and as background — a marsh that suddenly goes quiet has told the party something.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (13): 1d-7 crushing, Reach C. It eats flies. This entry is included for completeness.

notes: Racial cost: -158 points of traits plus 5 points of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Crab
monsters.pageRef: Giant Crab (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A flooded sea cave or sunken wreck, floored with cracked shell and picked bone.

description.text: A crab the size of a war shield, clattering out of the surf onto stone. The shell shrugs off a sword cut and the claws will take a hand off at the wrist. It is slow and stupid, and coming at it from the front is still a poor idea.

attacks.name: Pincer
attacks.notes: Pincer (12): 1d cutting, Reach C. Takes hold and does not open again while the crab lives. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: -33 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Lizard
monsters.pageRef: Giant Lizard (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A rock cleft or cave mouth warmed by the afternoon sun, littered with shed skin.

description.text: A monitor grown to the length of a horse, tasting the air with a forked tongue and climbing a cave wall as readily as it crosses the floor. Deep folk keep them as mounts and pack animals. Wild ones are unhurried and unfrightened, and they will eat a person if the opportunity is convenient.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. A filthy wound; bites that do not kill often fester.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (14): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: -46 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Sea Horse
monsters.pageRef: Giant Sea Horse (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: Kelp forest and reef shallows, anchored by the tail to whatever holds still.

description.text: Sea elves and sahuagin both ride these, and a good one costs more than a good horse. It is armored in bony rings, placid to the point of stubbornness, and slower than most things that would like to eat it. Handled well it will carry a rider all day. Handled badly it simply stops.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Ram (13): 1d+2 crushing, Reach C. Driven with the whole body; the armored snout is the only part of it built to hit anything.

notes: Racial cost: -39 points of traits plus 1 point of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Toad
monsters.pageRef: Giant Toad (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A wallow under a rotting log at the edge of standing water.

description.text: A toad the size of a hound, sitting so still among the reeds that it reads as a stone until the tongue comes out. It swallows anything it can fit, which at this size includes a halfling. The skin sweats a poison that punishes anyone who grabs it barehanded, though it is a bad hour rather than a death.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-2 crushing, Reach C. The toad swallows what it can and works on the rest.

attacks.name: Tongue
attacks.notes: Tongue (14): 1d-3 crushing, Reach C,1. Lashes out a hex, sticks, and drags a lighter target into reach of the mouth.

attacks.name: Toxic Skin
attacks.notes: Toxic Skin: Reach C. Anything that bites or grapples the toad bare-handed rolls HT or is nauseated and blurred of vision for minutes. No attack roll; contact alone does it.

notes: Racial cost: -44 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.

attacks.notes: Talons (12): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: -46 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.

monsters.pageRef: Awakened Shrub (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: Wherever it was rooted when the spell found it, and a slow shuffling radius around that.

description.text: A waist-high bush that has been given a mind and, unluckily for it, a clear understanding of its position. It talks, it remembers who planted it, and it cannot defend itself against anybody with an axe. Most awakened shrubs end up as somebody's informant.

attacks.name: Rake
attacks.notes: Rake (8): 1d-5 cutting, Reach C. Thorns dragged across whatever is in reach. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 0 points of traits plus 1 point of skills.
An awakened plant is awake in the full sense and will hold a conversation, which is generally why it is in the scene at all.
Fire is the obvious answer to it. There is no vulnerability on the stat block, so a GM should rule that at the table.

notes: Racial cost: 154 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.

attacks.notes: Bite (16): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -37 points of traits plus 14 points of skills.

monsters.name: Black Dragon Wyrmling
monsters.pageRef: Black Dragon Wyrmling (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A flooded cavern behind a waterfall or under a drowned ruin, reached by swimming.

description.text: Black dragons keep to swamp and drowned ruin. They are the meanest of the chromatic line — cruel without needing a reason, patient about it, content to let a place rot around them. The breath is acid, and it goes on working after it lands. A wyrmling is newly out of the shell and already the size of a warhorse. It has a full set of teeth and no judgement at all about when to use them.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d+1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (14): 1d+3 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (12): 1d+2 crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (12): 1d+1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Acid Breath
attacks.notes: Acid Breath (14): 3d corrosion, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of acid that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

notes: Racial cost: 304 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 18 at a sprint (primary); water Move 4.
Immunity to its own element covers that one damage type and nothing else, and it is not in the published DR. A red dragon is not armored against a sword by being immune to fire.

The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, and a dragon that could breathe every turn would be a different fight. The published rating does not yet discount it for that, so it runs high for the sixteen colors whose breath is their best attack, worst for the acid breathers. Read these dragons as somewhat less dangerous than the number says.

monsters.name: Adult Copper Dragon
monsters.pageRef: Adult Copper Dragon (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A dry hillside cave with a concealed entrance and at least two ways out.

description.text: Copper dragons are jokers, and the joke is usually on whoever came looking for the hoard. They are fast, hard to corner, and genuinely funny until the moment they stop being funny. The breath is acid. An adult has held its territory for centuries and knows every road and every lord in it. It worked out long ago what it would do if adventurers ever turned up, and none of what happens next is improvised.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 6d-1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (12): 6d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (10): 6d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (10): 6d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Acid Breath
attacks.notes: Acid Breath (12): 10d corrosion, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of acid that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defense; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: Racial cost: 640 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 24 at a sprint (primary).
Immunity to its own element covers that one damage type and nothing else, and it is not in the published DR. A red dragon is not armored against a sword by being immune to fire.

The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, and a dragon that could breathe every turn would be a different fight. The published rating does not yet discount it for that, so it runs high for the sixteen colors whose breath is their best attack, worst for the acid breathers. Read these dragons as somewhat less dangerous than the number says.
Extra Attack: an adult dragon bites and claws in the same turn, which is most of what makes it different from a very large animal.

monsters.name: Ancient Gold Dragon
monsters.pageRef: Ancient Gold Dragon (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: Somewhere unlikely and beautiful, kept plain, with the hoard behind a door it does not bother to lock.

description.text: Gold dragons are the ones the stories are actually about: wise, formal, and perfectly willing to end a threat rather than negotiate with it. They ask questions a party would rather not answer honestly. The breath is fire, and it comes out last. An ancient dragon is older than the kingdom it sleeps under and has outlived everyone who knew where it was. What follows is less a fight than a negotiation, conducted by something that worked out what the party wants, and what they will give up to get it, some while before they arrived.

attacks.name: Tail

attacks.name: Wing Buffet

attacks.name: Fire Breath
attacks.notes: Fire Breath (11): 15d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of fire that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

monsters.name: Aasimar
monsters.lair: A temple guest-cell, a border chapterhouse, or wherever the thing it came to stop is.

description.text: Somewhere back up the family line there was a celestial, and it shows: the eyes are wrong in a way nobody can quite place, and the hair holds light it was never given. Aasimar tend to end up with the errand nobody else will take, partly from conviction and partly because everyone assumes they will. Acid, cold and lightning all trouble them less than they should.

attacks.name: Longsword
attacks.notes: Longsword (11): 1d+1 cutting, Reach 1. Carried openly and drawn late. An aasimar would generally rather be talked out of using it.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.notes: Shield Bash (12): 1d-2 crushing, Reach 1. Used to move somebody out of a doorway rather than to hurt them.

notes: Racial cost: 98 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.
The inherited resistances cover one damage type each and are not in the published DR. An aasimar is not armored against a sword.
The daylight an aasimar can call once a day is not on the stat block. It lights a room and injures nobody; a GM should simply rule it.

monsters.pageRef: Bugbear (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A cave mouth or ruined gatehouse a day's walk from whatever it has been robbing.

description.text: Seven feet of goblin-kin with a hunter's patience and a bully's instincts. What surprises people is how quietly something that size moves. attacks.name: Javelin
attacks.notes: Javelin (13): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 15. Thrown to open an ambush, from the dark, at the person carrying the light.

monsters.pageRef: Centaur (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: Open grassland with wood at its edge, and no permanent structure worth the name.

description.text: Horse from the withers back, person from the withers up, and entirely one animal about it — a centaur does not ride, it runs. They are proud, easily offended, and better archers than anyone on foot should have to deal with, since they can shoot at a gallop and outrun whatever answers. Most trouble with centaurs starts with somebody crossing their grazing without asking.

attacks.notes: Lance (12): 2d+1 impaling, Reach 1,2. Couched and delivered at speed, which is the only way a centaur ever wants to fight.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (10): 2d+1 crushing, Reach C,1. Reared and brought down. Cannot parry.

monsters.pageRef: Drow (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A city carved into a cavern wall, reached by a road nobody surface-born has walked and returned from.

description.text: Elves of the deep places, as quick and long-lived and beautiful as the ones above, which is most of what makes them difficult. Drow open from darkness with poisoned bolts and come in afterwards to finish what the poison started. Magic thrown at them tends to slide off, they need no light at all, and full daylight leaves them squinting and furious.

attacks.notes: Hand Crossbow (13): 1d-1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. The bolt barely matters. What matters is what is on it: a target who takes any wound at all rolls against the poison or goes down asleep where they stand.

attacks.name: Shortsword
attacks.notes: Shortsword (13): 1d cutting, Reach 1. Used to finish, in the dark, on somebody who is already having a bad time.

notes: Racial cost: 89 points of traits plus 32 points of skills.

monsters.name: Duergar
monsters.pageRef: Duergar (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A fortified working built by people who were taken there to build it.

description.text: Gray, hairless dwarves who kept the craft and lost everything else. Duergar work their mines with slave labor, resent every hour of it, and carry a joylessness that reads as menace long before anyone draws. They can also stop being visible, which they do without ceremony and about four seconds before it matters.

attacks.name: War Pick
attacks.notes: War Pick (12): 1d+2 impaling, Reach 1. Punched through mail. Duergar generally open the fight already invisible and standing closer than anyone believed possible.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.notes: Shield Bash (12): 1d-1 crushing, Reach 1. Used to pin somebody against the gallery wall while the pick works.

notes: Racial cost: 102 points of traits plus 24 points of skills.
The enlargement a duergar can call is not on the stat block. It changes size, Strength and reach for a few minutes, and running it is the GM's job.
Mail and a heavy shield are the usual kit and are not in this record's DR.
The encounter figure of eight is the creature. A goblin on its own behaves like a different monster and should be run as one.

monsters.name: Forest Gnome
monsters.pageRef: Forest Gnome (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5)
monsters.lair: A hollow under a root ball, with a door nobody who was not shown it has ever found.

description.text: The smallest gnomes and the least interested in being found. A forest gnome can stand three paces from a hunting party and pass for undergrowth as long as it cares to, and it is on speaking terms with the animals that then decline to point anyone in the right direction. They are friendly enough once met. That is a decision they make, not one made for them.

attacks.name: Sling
attacks.notes: Sling (11): 1d-3 crushing, Reach Ranged, 60. Loosed from cover, at range, by somebody who has already worked out where to be next.

attacks.name: Small Knife
attacks.notes: Small Knife (12): 1d-4 impaling, Reach C,1. A last resort, and the forest gnome knows it.

notes: Racial cost: 28 points of traits plus 30 points of skills.

monsters.lair: Whatever was standing there before the pack arrived, now roofless and stinking.

description.text: Hyena-headed raiders who hunt in packs and take the long way around to come in behind. attacks.name: Shortbow
attacks.notes: Shortbow (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. Loosed at anything running away. The damage is the bow's.

monsters.pageRef: Goblin (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A warren behind somebody else's ruin, entered through a hole cut too small for a man in mail.

description.text: Small, sour and numerous. One goblin is a nuisance and runs at the first real hit. Twelve of them in a tunnel they dug themselves, with spears and a hole in the ceiling, are a serious afternoon. They are not brave and they know it, so they do not fight anywhere they have not arranged in advance.

attacks.name: Spear

attacks.name: Shortbow
attacks.notes: Shortbow (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. Loosed in volleys from a gallery nobody looked up at. The damage is the bow's.

monsters.pageRef: Gray Elf (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5)
monsters.lair: A hall on a high valley shoulder, older than the road up to it and harder to find than either.

description.text: The high, thin, silver-haired kind, and the most insufferable. Gray elves live in mountain valleys reading things nobody else can, decline to explain themselves, and are genuinely as clever as they behave. They are also slight, and quite aware that this is why they took up magic. Spells cast at one tend to slide off.

attacks.notes: Longsword (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach 1. Worn as a matter of form for a century at a time, and still perfectly well handled.

notes: Racial cost: 79 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.
The spell list is the GM's to assign. What is here is the racial template, not any particular oni's education.

description.text: Human enough to live in a human town and elven enough that nobody there forgets it. monsters.name: Half-Orc
monsters.lair: A barracks, a caravan guard's tent, or the far end of whichever bar will serve them.

description.text: Stronger and tougher than a man, and treated worse than either parent's people would treat a stranger. Half-orcs make excellent soldiers and are hired as such by everyone who then declines to drink with them. The temper is real and mostly earned, and it is why the arrangement rarely lasts a season.

attacks.name: Battleaxe

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.notes: Punch (12): 1d-1 crushing, Reach C. Thrown far more often than the axe, and usually in a room where the axe would be unwelcome.

notes: Racial cost: -14 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.

monsters.name: Hobgoblin
monsters.pageRef: Hobgoblin (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A fort with cleared ground in front of it, a watch roster, and a gate that is actually shut.

description.text: The goblinoid that got organized. Hobgoblins drill, post sentries, hold a line when it is losing and rotate the front rank while they do it, so six of them are a harder problem than twenty goblins and a much worse surprise. They are not frightened of adventurers. They have a standing plan for adventurers.

attacks.name: Longsword
attacks.notes: Longsword (13): 1d+3 cutting, Reach 1. Drilled with, maintained, and used in a line with somebody else's shield on the flank.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.notes: Shield Bash (13): 1d-1 crushing, Reach 1. The line steps forward together. This is what steps forward first.

attacks.name: Longbow
attacks.notes: Longbow (12): 1d+2 impaling, Reach Ranged, 200. Volleyed on command from the rank behind. The damage is the bow's.

notes: Racial cost: 79 points of traits plus 22 points of skills.
Mail and a shield are standard issue and are not in this record's DR, so a hobgoblin met in the field is better protected than the stat block says.

monsters.name: Kobold
monsters.pageRef: Kobold (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A mine they dug themselves, in which every third corridor is a mistake to walk down.

description.text: Knee-high scaled things with dog-like snouts, and by some distance the best military engineers in any dungeon. A kobold in a fair fight is nothing. Kobolds do not have fair fights — they have pits, deadfalls, thirty of themselves, and a corridor whose safe route they know. Cold slows them and daylight makes them miserable.

attacks.name: Spear
attacks.notes: Spear (12): 1d-2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Held at the far end and used from behind whatever is in the way.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 1d-4 cutting, Reach C. What is left when the spear has been dropped and the corridor is full.

attacks.name: Sling
attacks.notes: Sling (11): 1d-3 crushing, Reach Ranged, 60. From a ledge, in the dark, at a party already dealing with something else.

notes: Racial cost: -14 points of traits plus 26 points of skills.
Kobolds are reptiles. A cold gallery genuinely slows them down.

monsters.name: Lizardfolk
monsters.pageRef: Lizardfolk (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A village of stilt huts over black water, reached by a channel only a flat boat clears.

description.text: Scaled, tailed and entirely at home in water a person would drown in. Lizardfolk hunt from below, hold their breath for minutes together, and come up under a boat rather than alongside it. They are not cruel and not much interested in anyone else's business, which holds exactly as long as nobody hunts their stretch of marsh.

attacks.name: Barbed Spear
attacks.notes: Barbed Spear (11): 1d+2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Fire-hardened, barbed for fish and entirely adequate for the other thing.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Delivered in the water, on something already being held under.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (10): 1d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc at knee height. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 49 points of traits plus 22 points of skills.
DR 2 is scale rather than armor, so a scratch that only needs skin contact still gets through. Lizardfolk wear nothing over it.

monsters.name: Merfolk
monsters.pageRef: Merfolk (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A reef terrace or a drowned harbor wall, built on rather than into.

description.text: People from the waist up and something with a tail below, living on reefs and in drowned places, and perfectly willing to talk to a ship that behaves. Merfolk breathe air and water equally well, so negotiations happen at the rail rather than underwater. On land they can drag themselves about, and they hate it.

attacks.name: Trident
attacks.notes: Trident (12): 1d+2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Held two-handed and driven upward, which is the direction merfolk fight from.

attacks.name: Thrown Spear
attacks.notes: Thrown Spear (12): 1d impaling, Reach Ranged, 15. Thrown through water at short range, where a bow would be useless.

notes: Racial cost: 73 points of traits plus 14 points of skills.

monsters.name: Merrow
monsters.pageRef: Merrow (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A flooded sea cave with a shingle shelf at the back, and bones on the shelf.

description.text: Ogres that went into the sea and got worse. A merrow is ten feet of green-gray muscle with a harpoon and a coil of rope, and its whole method is to put the barb into somebody at the rail and pull. They are not clever. They are patient in the way an ambush predator is patient, and a wreck is what they have been waiting for.

attacks.name: Harpoon

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (11): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Taken while the harpoon rope is still being hauled.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: Slam (10): 2d-1 crushing, Reach C,1. Delivered from below with the whole mass behind it, in water, where nobody has footing.

notes: Racial cost: 84 points of traits plus 10 points of skills.

monsters.pageRef: Ogre (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A cave with a fire outside it and the remains of several carts scattered downhill.

description.text: Ten feet of appetite with a club. Ogres are slow, stupid, foul-tempered and enormously strong, and a fight with one comes down to arithmetic: sooner or later it connects, and whoever it connects with stops being a combatant. They take a toll on roads, eat what they take, and do not entertain a second offer.

attacks.name: Greatclub

monsters.name: Oni
monsters.pageRef: Oni (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5: Ogre Mage, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A house in a mountain village where the previous family is not discussed.

description.text: An ogre with a sorcerer's education and centuries of practice at being somebody's neighbor. In its own shape it is a horned blue giant with a glaive. In the shape it usually wears it is a well-liked man in a mountain village. It flies, it vanishes, it heals whatever is done to it, and it would much rather charm the guard than fight the party.

attacks.name: Glaive
attacks.notes: Glaive (13): 4d+3 cutting, Reach 1,2. Kept on the wall of the house it took, and reached for without changing shape first.

attacks.name: Cone of Cold
attacks.notes: Cone of Cold (14): 6d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A breath of killing cold across the front arc. It costs the oni to use and cannot be repeated every second.

attacks.name: Charm
attacks.notes: Charm: Reach Ranged, 10. One person is told to stop, and rolls against Will to not. The oni much prefers this to the glaive, because a charmed guard opens the door.

notes: Racial cost: 437 points of traits plus 40 points of skills.
Oni in SRD 5.1 and Ogre Mage in SRD 3.5 are one creature, and this is both. The flight comes from the older heading and is kept.
The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second; the published rating does not yet discount it for that.

monsters.name: Orc
monsters.pageRef: Orc (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A stockade round a stolen village, or a gallery in somebody else's mine.

description.text: Broad, gray-skinned and permanently furious. Orcs raid because raiding is the shape their society has settled into and because they enjoy it. They come in numbers, close immediately, and keep coming well past the point a sensible band would have withdrawn. Daylight leaves them squinting, so the attack is nearly always at dusk.

attacks.name: Falchion
attacks.notes: Falchion (12): 2d+1 cutting, Reach 1. Heavy, badly balanced and swung by an arm that does not care.

attacks.name: Javelin
attacks.notes: Javelin (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 20. Thrown once at the charge, then forgotten about.

attacks.name: Fist
attacks.notes: Fist (11): 1d crushing, Reach C. Used on other orcs about as often as on anyone else.

notes: Racial cost: 7 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Mail scraps and a shield are common and are not in this record's DR.
The camouflage and non-detection a svirfneblin can call are not on the stat block. Both come and go, and a GM should rule them.

monsters.name: Sprite
monsters.pageRef: Sprite (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A clearing nobody finds twice, somewhere in old wood.

description.text: A hand-span of winged fey with a bow and no fear at all. A sprite can stop being visible, hovers where nothing can reach it, and knows the wood better than anything walking through it. The arrows do no damage worth the name. What is on them puts a grown soldier to sleep where they stand.

attacks.name: Sprite Bow
attacks.notes: Sprite Bow (16): 1d-4 impaling, Reach Ranged, 40. The arrow is the size of a pin and the wound is nothing. What is on the point puts a grown soldier to sleep for an hour.

attacks.name: Needle Sword
attacks.notes: Needle Sword (15): 1d-6 impaling, Reach C. Genuinely a threat only to something the sprite's own size, and drawn with complete confidence regardless.

notes: Racial cost: 84 points of traits plus 30 points of skills.

monsters.pageRef: Svirfneblin (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A warren of low galleries with three ways out of every room, and gemstones in the walls.

description.text: Deep gnomes: gray, wiry, and the most cautious folk under any mountain. Svirfneblin live between the dwarven holds and worse neighbors, and have survived it by never once being where anyone expected. attacks.notes: Hand Crossbow (12): 1d-1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. Loosed once from cover and not reloaded. The damage is the weapon's.

monsters.name: Tallfellow Halfling
monsters.pageRef: Tallfellow Halfling (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5)
monsters.lair: A farm on good ground, with elves for neighbors and a hedge nobody sees over.

description.text: The tall halflings, a head above their cousins, which still leaves them looking up at everybody else. Tallfellows farm good open ground and get on unusually well with elves. They are better archers and better sneaks than their reputation for pastoral harmlessness suggests, they see a long way, and they say very little about what they have seen.

attacks.name: Large Knife
attacks.notes: Large Knife (13): 1d-3 cutting, Reach C,1. A hedging tool with a very good edge.

notes: Racial cost: 37 points of traits plus 32 points of skills.

monsters.name: Tiefling
monsters.lair: Two streets away from wherever the last misunderstanding happened.

description.text: Somebody with a fiend in the family, and everybody can tell. Tieflings run to horns, unsettling eyes, and a tail kept under a coat, and they spend their lives being blamed first. Most respond by getting very good at leaving, at talking, and at taking what they were going to be accused of taking anyway. Fire, cold and lightning trouble them less than they should.

attacks.name: Shortsword
attacks.notes: Shortsword (12): 1d cutting, Reach 1. Drawn in an alley, generally in the second half of a conversation that started politely.

attacks.name: Knife
attacks.notes: Knife (13): 1d-2 impaling, Reach C,1. The one that was already in the hand.

notes: Racial cost: 84 points of traits plus 24 points of skills.

monsters.name: Wild Elf
monsters.pageRef: Wild Elf (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5)
monsters.lair: No settlement at all: a range of deep forest and a set of camps used in rotation.

description.text: Elves who never built anything and see no reason to start. Wild elves range deep forest in bands, hunt with stone-headed spears and bows nobody hears drawn, and regard every other kind of elf as a disappointment. attacks.notes: Longbow (15): 1d+2 impaling, Reach Ranged, 200. The first anyone knows about a wild elf. The damage is the bow's.

attacks.name: Spear
attacks.notes: Spear (13): 1d impaling, Reach 1,2. Stone-headed, and quite good enough for anything that got this close.

notes: Racial cost: 76 points of traits plus 40 points of skills.

attacks.name: Longsword

monsters.name: Cheetah
monsters.lair: A shaded scrape in tall grass where cubs are left while the mother hunts.

description.text: The fastest thing on four legs, and the least able to keep it up. A cheetah stalks to within a hundred yards, then spends everything it has in a few seconds, knocking its quarry off its feet at the end of the run. Caught at that moment it is exhausted and light-boned, and it will give up the kill rather than fight for it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (16): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Aimed at the throat once the quarry is down.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (16): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Used to trip a running target rather than to wound. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 18 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 24 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Death Dog
monsters.pageRef: Death Dog (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A fouled dry wash or ruin littered with the picked-over remains of travelers.

description.text: A two-headed hound the color of dust, running the dry country in pairs and hating everything that walks upright. Both heads bite and both heads watch, so there is no blind side to approach from. What kills travelers is rarely the wound. It is what grows in the wound afterwards, slowly and visibly, and it does not stop on its own.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Anyone bitten rolls HT. On a failure the wound will not close: it goes gray at the edges and spreads, costing 1 HP a day until the rot is cured by magic or by cutting well past the margin. The lost HP does not return until the disease is stopped.

notes: Racial cost: 38 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.

monsters.name: Dire Wolf
monsters.pageRef: Dire Wolf (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A cave mouth or undercut bank fouled with bone, held by the whole pack.

description.text: A wolf grown to the size of a pony, hunting in packs that work a treeline the way soldiers work a hedgerow. They circle, they cut off the slowest, and they take turns. One is a serious fight. Four have already picked somebody.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d+1 cutting, Reach C. A dire wolf bites low and drives, trying to put its target on the ground for the rest of the pack.

notes: Racial cost: 10 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 12 at a sprint (primary).
The pack is the threat. Run these as a coordinated group, not as four separate rolls.

monsters.name: Dog
monsters.lair: A yard, a doorway, or the lee side of whatever building feeds it.

description.text: The ordinary working dog of farm and street: forty pounds of noise and nose. On its own it is barely a combatant, and what it is for is warning, tracking and company. Village strays run in loose packs and will follow a party for miles on the chance of scraps.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-4 cutting, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -69 points of traits plus 14 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 9 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Donkey
monsters.lair: None; a donkey belongs to whatever holding or caravan owns its lead rope.

description.text: Short, patient and surefooted, carrying a third of its own weight up tracks a horse would refuse. It eats what it finds, drinks little, and stops dead when it judges the next step unsafe. Handlers call that stubbornness. More of them have been saved by it than killed by it.

attacks.name: Kick
attacks.notes: Kick (8): 1d+3 crushing, Reach C,1.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (10): 1d crushing, Reach C. Only when it has no way out.

notes: Racial cost: -46 points of traits plus 1 point of skills.

monsters.name: Elephant
monsters.pageRef: Elephant (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: None; a herd walks a circuit between water and forage and holds no fixed ground.

description.text: Seven tons of animal that is not remotely stupid, moving in a family group led by the oldest cow. Left alone it ignores people entirely. Provoked, or separated from a calf, it comes forward at a speed nothing that size should manage, and it does not need the tusks to settle the argument.

attacks.name: Tusks
attacks.notes: Tusks (10): 5d impaling, Reach C,1.

attacks.name: Trample
attacks.notes: Trample (8): 5d crushing, Reach C. Against a target already down.

attacks.name: Trunk
attacks.notes: Trunk (10): 5d-1 crushing, Reach C,1. Also used to grab and throw.

notes: Racial cost: 176 points of traits plus 2 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Elk
monsters.lair: Open woodland edge and high meadow; the herd beds where it grazes.

description.text: A deer the size of a horse, carrying a rack wide enough to catch on branches. Out of season it is meat that runs away. In the rut a bull is loud, sleepless and looking for something to fight, and a party crossing his meadow will do.

attacks.name: Antlers
attacks.notes: Antlers (12): 2d impaling, Reach C,1.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (10): 2d+2 crushing, Reach C,1. Front hooves, brought down on a target that has gone down.

notes: Racial cost: -11 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5, 10 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Badger
monsters.pageRef: Giant Badger (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A dug sett of packed earth tunnels with several bolt holes, extended every year.

description.text: Low, wide and built entirely out of bad attitude, with digging claws that go through packed earth and will do the same to a boot. It would rather be underground than anywhere else. A party that opens up its sett gets everything the badger has, immediately, without a warning growl.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (13): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Digging claws, as long as a knife. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (13): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -32 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Boar
monsters.pageRef: Giant Boar (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A wallow the size of a cart, ringed by uprooted saplings and churned mud.

description.text: A boar the size of a plow horse, with hide over the shoulders that turns a spear point and a temper that has never once improved. It charges the moment it is sure, keeps going through the first wound, and is generally still coming when whoever stood the ground has reconsidered.

attacks.name: Tusks
attacks.notes: Tusks (12): 2d impaling, Reach C,1. Tusks the length of a forearm, driven upward on the charge.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 2d-1 cutting, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -10 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Elk
monsters.pageRef: Giant Elk (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: Deep old forest and high valleys, far from any road.

description.text: Rare enough that seeing one counts as a sign rather than a sighting. It stands taller at the shoulder than a mounted rider, moves through heavy timber without hurrying, and watches a party with something closer to judgement than fear. Killing one is legal almost nowhere and forgiven almost never.

attacks.notes: Antlers (14): 3d-1 impaling, Reach C,2.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (12): 3d+2 crushing, Reach C,1. Against a target already down.

notes: Racial cost: 81 points of traits plus 8 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 12 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Goat
monsters.pageRef: Giant Goat (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: Ledges and scree above the tree line, on ground nothing else will stand on.

description.text: An ill-tempered mountain goat the size of a pony, standing on ledges that have no business holding it. Hill folk keep them for milk and haulage and put up with the bruises. In the wild they defend a slope by ramming, and on bad footing the fall afterwards is worse than the hit.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Ram (12): 1d+2 crushing, Reach C. Delivered downhill wherever possible.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (10): 1d+3 crushing, Reach C,1.

notes: Racial cost: -44 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Hyena
monsters.pageRef: Giant Hyena (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A den under a thorn thicket or ruin, floored with splintered bone.

description.text: Shoulder-high, sloped from front to back, and loud in the dark. Giant hyenas run in clans and are as happy taking a kill off something else as making their own. They will follow a caravan for days without closing, waiting for somebody to fall behind. The jaws go through bone as a matter of routine.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d+1 cutting, Reach C. Jaws built to crack marrow bone; armor straps and shield rims fare no better.

notes: Racial cost: -24 points of traits plus 8 points of skills.

monsters.name: Constrictor Snake
monsters.pageRef: Constrictor Snake (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A branch over a game trail, or a hollow under a root mass near water.

description.text: Ten feet of muscle that has never needed venom. It lies along a branch with its head down at about head height, waiting for something warm to pass underneath. Everything turns on the first second. Before the coils it is a snake; after them it is arithmetic.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Backward-curved teeth that take hold rather than cut. The bite is how the coils arrive.

attacks.name: Constrict
attacks.notes: Constrict: Reach C. Once it has hold, the coils go on. No attack roll and no defense: win a Quick Contest of ST each second or take crushing damage and lose the breath to shout with.

notes: Racial cost: -22 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Constrictor Snake
monsters.pageRef: Giant Constrictor Snake (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A river bank undercut by the current, with a slide worn smooth into deep water.

description.text: Thirty feet of river snake that swallows deer whole and sees no reason a person should be different. It comes out of brown water without a sound, takes hold with the jaws, and has three coils on before anyone upstream notices the splash. There is no trick to fighting it, only how fast the coils are cut.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (13): 3d-2 cutting, Reach C,1. Takes hold of an arm, a leg or a head and does not open again.

attacks.name: Constrict
attacks.notes: Constrict: Reach C. No attack roll and no defense once it has hold. Win a Quick Contest of ST each second or take crushing damage; a failure also costs the victim the ability to breathe, and drowning follows if the snake takes it into the water.

notes: Racial cost: 8 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.

monsters.lair: A rock pile or ruin with sun on one side and a hole on the other.

description.text: Ten feet of snake carrying enough venom to kill a horse, striking from a coil faster than a hand can be pulled back. It has no interest in a fight it cannot win by chemistry, so it warns first. The ones that do not warn are the ones that kill people.

notes: Racial cost: -52 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.

monsters.pageRef: Giant Scorpion (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A scraped burrow under a slab, with the sand outside smoothed by its own passage.

description.text: Eight feet of black chitin that takes hold with the claws and takes its time with the tail. The shell turns most weapons and the pincers do not let go. The sting is what actually kills; everything before it is the scorpion arranging matters to suit itself.

attacks.notes: Sting (13): 1d+2 impaling, Reach C,1. Arched over the back and driven down. Roll HT or the limb goes numb, then the chest does; a second sting on a failed victim is usually the end of it.

attacks.name: Pincer
attacks.notes: Pincer (13): 1d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Grabs and holds the target still for the sting. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: -25 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.

monsters.name: Giant Spider
monsters.pageRef: Giant Spider (Monsters on Automatic; answers SRD 3.5: Monstrous Spider, SRD 5.1)
monsters.lair: A sheet of web strung across a shaft or a stand of trees, with wrapped bundles hanging in it.

description.text: A body the size of a large dog on a ten-foot span of legs, sitting motionless at the edge of its web where the light does not reach. It reads the whole web as one sense. It wants somebody held still, and most of that was arranged before anyone thought to look up.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d impaling, Reach C. Delivered to something already wrapped. Roll HT or go slack — the venom is meant to stop prey struggling, not to kill it outright.

attacks.name: Web
attacks.notes: Web: Reach 5. Thrown as a sheet from ambush. No damage; the target is stuck fast and must win a Quick Contest against the web's ST to tear free, and everything the spider does afterwards is against a target that cannot move. The web itself has DR 3 and can be cut or burned free; fire clears a hex of it in a turn and is by far the fastest answer.

notes: Racial cost: 8 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.
The 3.5 corpus prints 'Monstrous Spider' as a family of sizes rather than one creature; this record is the size that matches the 5.1 giant spider.
